The name Qahhar signifies a powerful, dominating, and victorious individual, one who is able to overcome all obstacles and challenges in life. Parents who choose Qahhar usually hope their child will grow to embody the conqueror and live with faith, good character and purpose.

He claimed to be the rightful Imam and gathered a large following of disenchanted Shia soldiers and peasants. historical_references.reference: Muhammad ibn Qahhar al-Bakri, a prominent 11th-century Andalusian explorer and geographer, who contributed significantly to the body of Islamic geographic knowledge. He traveled extensively throughout the Islamic world and wrote detailed accounts of his travels. His works were widely used by later geographers and scholars, and he is considered one of the pioneers of Islamic cartography.
